name: Tourism and hospitality
summary: Tourism is gaining momentum: the Ministry of Tourism reported more than 1.2 million international tourists and upwards of 2 billion US dollars in revenue over the nine months reported on April 1, 2026, alongside over 30 million domestic travelers. Ethiopian Airlines carried 19.0 million passengers and earned $7.6 billion in the fiscal year to June 2025, and the African Development Bank is lead arranger for nearly $8 billion of the $10 billion Bishoftu airport, a project it describes as set to be Africa's largest airport by 2029. Star-rated hotels, lodges, MICE facilities and tourist transport are open to foreign investors, with income tax exemptions and duty-free import of capital goods available for new enterprises.

The closest published indicators included are National Bank of Ethiopia Treasury bill yields (12.3 percent for all tenors and 11.0 percent for 91-day bills in May 2026) and the economy-wide bank lending rate (average 14.25 percent, range 7.00 to 21.50 percent, in 2023/24).

opportunities.title: Star-rated hotels and lodges
opportunities.detail: The Ministry of Tourism lists star-rated tourist hotels and lodges, entertainment and shopping centers, food and beverage, leisure and sports, and tourism medical services as open to foreign investors.

opportunities.title: MICE and conference tourism
opportunities.detail: The Ministry of Tourism promotes Addis Ababa venues for events from ten to a few thousand delegates, including the AU Conference Centre and the Addis Ababa International Convention and Exhibition Center, which is under development on 11 hectares.

opportunities.title: New destination projects
opportunities.detail: The investment commission invites investors to join government-launched destination projects at Gorgora, Wonchi and Koisha, and lists hotels and resorts, convention centers, duty-free centers and cultural villages as opportunities.

opportunities.title: Bishoftu airport hub
opportunities.detail: The $10 billion Bishoftu International Airport, 40 km south of Addis Ababa, is planned for 60 million passengers initially and 110 million eventually, with Phase I completion expected in November 2029; AfDB is mandated lead arranger for nearly $8 billion and plans $500 million of its own financing, subject to Board approval.

opportunities.title: Heritage and urban tourism
opportunities.detail: The Ministry of Tourism cites the Dine for Nation destinations and restoration of Harar Jugol and Fasil Ghebbi as government priorities.

incentives.detail: Tourism is listed among Ethiopia's priority economic sectors, and investors establishing a new enterprise are entitled to an income tax exemption that depends on the investment sub-sector.

Investors may import duty-free capital goods and construction materials to establish a new enterprise; in sectors other than manufacturing and agriculture, investors with at least USD 200,000 and 50 permanent Ethiopian jobs may import duty-free capital goods for up to 5 years.
The Ministry of Tourism offers pre- and post-bid assistance, convention planning support and on-site services to organizers bringing international events to Ethiopia.

risks.detail: Investment rules differ by segment: star-rated hotels and lodges are open to foreign investors, while non-star hotels, lodges, guest houses, restaurants, travel agencies, ticket sales and tour operation are reserved for domestic investors, and foreign investors may hold up to 49 percent in domestic air transport.

Institutional set-up is being updated: a draft proclamation discussed in parliament in October 2026 would re-establish the Ministry of Tourism as the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, so investors should confirm their counterpart ministry.

Bishoftu airport timelines depend on financing approvals and site preparation: the AfDB financing remained subject to Board approval at signing, and the project includes a $350 million resettlement and livelihood restoration allocation.
